elements.element: No liquidated damages are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) continues to require the Company to pay a Termination Payment, and the added sentence expressly characterizes that payment as a “liquidated amount.”

elements.element: No penalties are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not separately impose or identify any penalty payable by the Company; the termination payment is characterized as a liquidated amount and early-termination fee.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer is capped at three (3) months' fees.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence states that the Termination Payment and early-termination fee “in no event shall exceed three (3) months' fees.”

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence states that the Termination Payment is “the sole liquidated amount and early-termination fee payable by the Company under this Agreement.”

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because it preserves an express liquidated termination payment. It does achieve the fallback by making that payment the sole liquidated amount/early-termination fee and imposing a three-month cap. The change is limited to what is needed for the fallback and leaves the existing formula and installment mechanics operative, subject to the cap. Drafting quality is reduced because “three (3) months' fees” is undefined and may be difficult to apply to a payment otherwise calculated by reference to Net Sales.
